description:
What Is It?

Allulose is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the “sugar alcohol” family, which means it’s derived naturally from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, allulose does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. That makes it a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Allulose VS Sugar

Allulose is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike many sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some people say there is a mild cooling sensation instead. However, while sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, allulose is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love allulose. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but allulose is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using allulose in place of sugar. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers.

How Do You Use It?

You can use confectioners Allulose just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of granular allulose for every 1 cup of sugar found in a recipe. A teaspoon or two in your morning coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use allulose to your specific taste.

KAL 브랜드는 85년 동안 적절한 성분으로 적절한 보충제를 제조해왔습니다. 1932년부터 저희는 고객의 건강과 웰빙을 지원하는 최고 품질의 영양소를 전 세계에 모색했습니다. 선도적인 영양 연구를 저희의 지속적인 가이드로 활용하여, 당사의 증거 기반 접근 방식은 최고의 제품을 제공하기 위해 신뢰하는 브랜드에서 필요한 것을 찾는 충성스러운 고객을 만듭니다.

About Xylitol - A Great Choice For DIABETICS

Xylitol is a natural occurring polyalcohol found in most plants, fruits, vegetables and hardwoods. It has a similar sweetness to regular sugar but has 40% fewer calories. Interestingly, while technically a carbohydrate, xylitol is classed as low-carb as it does not contain fructose and hence has minimal impact on blood sugar levels. This makes xylitol a natural alternative for diabetics with its glycaemia index rating of only 7 vs 60-70 for regular sugar.

We recommend that xylitol products be used in a 1 part xylitol to 1 part sugar equivalent. Not recommended for baking situations where raising is needed -eg breads. Excessive consumption of xylitol in adults and children may induce a mild laxative effect so please use in moderation and as recommended.

DO NOT SERVE XYLITOL OR ANY PRODUCTS CONTAINING XYLITOL TO PETS.

What Is It?

Allulose is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the “sugar alcohol” family, which means it’s derived naturally from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, allulose does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. That makes it a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Allulose VS Sugar

Allulose is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike many sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some people say there is a mild cooling sensation instead. However, while sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, allulose is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love allulose. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but allulose is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using allulose in place of sugar. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers.

How Do You Use It?

You can use confectioners Allulose just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of granular allulose for every 1 cup of sugar found in a recipe. A teaspoon or two in your morning coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use allulose to your specific taste.

Xylitol is a perfect sugar alternative because it has so many health benefits, but it's also the same exact sweetness and appearance as table sugar so it is a spoon for spoon, cup for cup replacement for traditional sugar. This specific product is unique in that it is a finer granule size. Most xylitol is larger granule and people sometimes complain that it doesn't dissolve or bake as easily as sugar. This fine grain birch xylitol will alleviate those complaints. It is also important to note that all xylitol is not identical. Most xylitol is derived from corn, and furthermore, most xylitol is imported from China. All of our xylitol is actually produced in the United States using only North American hardwood as the source. Often called birch xylitol, birch bark xylitol, or birch sugar, these are all interchangeable names for the same product. Enjoy this premium product today.

description: Erythritol is 70% as sweet as table sugar, so you can use it as a cup for cup (1:1) replacement for sugar in recipes. The result will be slightly less sweet than sugar. Use a little more if more sweetness is desired. What Is Erythritol? Erythritol is naturally occurring in nature, found in small amounts in foods like grapes, melons and mushrooms, and in fermented foods such as wine, cheese and soy sauce. How Is It Made? Usually made from the naturally occurring sugars in plants, that sugar is mixed with water and then fermented with a natural culture. This natural fermentation process yields erythritol, which is then filtered, allowed to crystallize and then dried. The result is a granular form that looks very similar to table sugar and is ready to use as a table top sweetener. Why Use Erythritol? It has almost no calories. Erythritol has not been found to affect blood sugar or insulin levels and has a zero glycemic index, making it perfect for diabetics or those on a low carb dietary program. description:
Stevia, (Stevia rebaudiana), also called sweet leaf, flowering plant in the aster family (Asteraceae), grown for its sweet-tasting leaves. The plant is native to Paraguay, where it has a long history of use by the Guaraní people. The leaves contain a number of sweet-tasting known as steviol glycosides, which can be used fresh or dried to sweeten beverages or desserts or can be commercially processed into powdered noncaloric sweeteners.
Steviol glycosides, particularly the stevioside and rebaudioside A, can be more than 300 times sweeter than table sugar and are nonglycemic. Touted as a healthier alternative to sugar, stevia sweeteners grew in popularity worldwide in the early 21st century.
Stevia is a tender perennial herb that reaches 30.5–80 cm (1–2.5 feet) in height. The oblong aromatic leaves are 2.5 cm (1 inch) long with a prominent midrib and are arranged oppositely along the stems. The small tubular flowers have five white petals and are borne in terminal clusters; the flowers are usually removed to improve the flavour of the leaves. Germination from seed is difficult, and most plants are grown from cuttings. The plant requires rich well-drained soil and thrives in warm humid climates.
Stevia leaves have been used for more than 1,500 years by the Guaraní people. Traditionally, the plant was used to sweeten yerba maté and other teas, and it had a number of applications in folk medicine. The first scientific record of the plant dates to 1899, when Swiss botanist Mosè Giacomo Bertoni (known in Spanish as Moisés Santiago Bertoni) announced his discovery of the sweet-tasting plant and named it Eupatorium rebaudianum. In the early 1970s Japanese scientists developed the first commercial stevia-derived sweetener, which quickly gained popularity in that country.

About Xylitol - A Great Choice For DIABETICS

Xylitol is a natural occurring polyalcohol found in most plants, fruits, vegetables and hardwoods. It has a similar sweetness to regular sugar but has 40% fewer calories. Interestingly, while technically a carbohydrate, xylitol is classed as low-carb as it does not contain fructose and hence has minimal impact on blood sugar levels. This makes xylitol a natural alternative for diabetics with its glycaemia index rating of only 7 vs 60-70 for regular sugar.

We recommend that xylitol products be used in a 1 part xylitol to 1 part sugar equivalent. Not recommended for baking situations where raising is needed -eg breads. Excessive consumption of xylitol in adults and children may induce a mild laxative effect so please use in moderation and as recommended.

description:
What Is It?

Erythritol is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the “sugar alcohol” family, which means it’s derived naturally from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, erythritol does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. That makes it a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Erythritol VS Sugar

Erythritol is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike many sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some people say there is a mild cooling sensation instead. However, while sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, erythritol is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love erythritol. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but erythritol is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using erythritol in place of sugar. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers.

How Do You Use It?

You can use confectioners erythritol just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of powdered erythritol for every 1 cup of powdered sugar found in a recipe. A teaspoon or two in your morning coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use erythritol to your specific taste.

Yacon Syrup is a delicious sweetener that is extracted from the tuberous roots of the yacon plant (Smallanthus Sonchifolius), which is indigenous to the Andes mountains, located in South America. description:
Stevia, (Stevia rebaudiana), also called sweet leaf, flowering plant in the aster family (Asteraceae), grown for its sweet-tasting leaves. The plant is native to Paraguay, where it has a long history of use by the Guaraní people. The leaves contain a number of sweet-tasting known as steviol glycosides, which can be used fresh or dried to sweeten beverages or desserts or can be commercially processed into powdered noncaloric sweeteners.
Steviol glycosides, particularly the stevioside and rebaudioside A, can be more than 300 times sweeter than table sugar and are nonglycemic. Touted as a healthier alternative to sugar, stevia sweeteners grew in popularity worldwide in the early 21st century.
Stevia is a tender perennial herb that reaches 30.5–80 cm (1–2.5 feet) in height. The oblong aromatic leaves are 2.5 cm (1 inch) long with a prominent midrib and are arranged oppositely along the stems. The small tubular flowers have five white petals and are borne in terminal clusters; the flowers are usually removed to improve the flavour of the leaves. Germination from seed is difficult, and most plants are grown from cuttings. The plant requires rich well-drained soil and thrives in warm humid climates.
Stevia leaves have been used for more than 1,500 years by the Guaraní people. Traditionally, the plant was used to sweeten yerba maté and other teas, and it had a number of applications in folk medicine. The first scientific record of the plant dates to 1899, when Swiss botanist Mosè Giacomo Bertoni (known in Spanish as Moisés Santiago Bertoni) announced his discovery of the sweet-tasting plant and named it Eupatorium rebaudianum. In the early 1970s Japanese scientists developed the first commercial stevia-derived sweetener, which quickly gained popularity in that country.

About Xylitol - A Great Choice For DIABETICS

Xylitol is a natural occurring polyalcohol found in most plants, fruits, vegetables and hardwoods. It has a similar sweetness to regular sugar but has 40% fewer calories. Interestingly, while technically a carbohydrate, xylitol is classed as low-carb as it does not contain fructose and hence has minimal impact on blood sugar levels. This makes xylitol a natural alternative for diabetics with its glycaemia index rating of only 7 vs 60-70 for regular sugar.

We recommend that xylitol products be used in a 1 part xylitol to 1 part sugar equivalent. Not recommended for baking situations where raising is needed -eg breads. Excessive consumption of xylitol in adults and children may induce a mild laxative effect so please use in moderation and as recommended.

DO NOT SERVE XYLITOL OR ANY PRODUCTS CONTAINING XYLITOL TO PETS.

description: Cid Botanicals is a Miami-based, family owned health and wellness company. In 2004, we began our mission to provide the best botanical traditions and ancestral knowledge from around the globe, making them accessible to all. As a family company, Cid Botanicals strives to understand every last detail of the stevia process, from farm to your coffee cup. Our stevia starts off as a plant, growing in the fertile farms of Paraguay five hours outside of the capital, Asunción. The Paraguayan farmers have grown and used stevia for decades, using only the safest natural techniques to ensure the best quality stevia sweeteners. This includes using bees as natural pest control instead of chemicals. From there, our partners create a powder extract using a water extraction method that utilizes the whole leaf, not just one molecule such as Reb-A. Many sweeteners and sugar substitutes begin their process in a lab, ours starts on a farm. Because stevia is a natural plant, and because Cid Botanicals uses a whole-leaf extract, we minimize the amount of processing required to create a sweet, tasty sugar substitute. The stevia plant has been used for hundreds of years by the Guaraní people to sweeten their yerba mate tea. Long before we became concerned with low calorie sweeteners or faced a need for diabetic friendly products, the Guaraní discovered the delicious sweetness of stevia. For this reason many people see stevia as one of the safest natural sugar substitutes. Cid Botanicals stevia is not only a great way for diabetics and other health conscious consumers to cut calories, it’s also the best tasting stevia on earth.

description:
What Is It?

Erythritol is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the “sugar alcohol” family, which means it’s derived naturally from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, erythritol does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. That makes it a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Erythritol VS Sugar

Erythritol is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike many sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some people say there is a mild cooling sensation instead. However, while sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, erythritol is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love erythritol. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but erythritol is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using erythritol in place of sugar. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers.

How Do You Use It?

You can use confectioners erythritol just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of powdered erythritol for every 1 cup of powdered sugar found in a recipe. A teaspoon or two in your morning coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use erythritol to your specific taste.

Os muitos benefícios para a saúde do xarope de yacon Happy Iris incluem: altas quantidades de oligossacarídeos (FOS). O xarope de raiz de Yacon é um baixo índice glicêmico. Recomendamos usar uma colher de chá do xarope como uma alternativa de açúcar até três vezes ao dia como substituição de açúcar, ou no lugar de mel, xarope de bordo ou melado.

description: Navitas Naturals Yacon Slices are made from an ancient South American tuber that tastes more like a fruit than a root. The raw yacon is grown on small family owned organic farms in the Oxapampa region of the Peruvian Andes. Once the orange-red flowers signal harvest, the roots are extracted from the fertile earth, washed, peeled, and sliced before being dehydrated at low temperatures to preserve the nutrients. Yacon’s greatest attribute is its naturally high content of inulin, a complex sugar that breaks down slowly into the sweet tasting but low-sugar fructooligosaccharides (FOS). Although yacon tastes sweet, the sugars from the inulin are not digestible and pass through the body. FOS also promotes the production of healthy probiotics within the body, which can contribute to better digestion and colon health. Yacon also contains amino acids, potassium, calcium, phosphorous and iron. This root food is known as the “apple of the earth” in Peru, so it is not surprising that Navitas Naturals Yacon Slices taste like a delicious, exotic apple. Eat them straight out of the bag or add them to cereals, oatmeal, baked goods and salads.

About Xylitol - A Great Choice For DIABETICS

Xylitol is a natural occurring polyalcohol found in most plants, fruits, vegetables and hardwoods. It has a similar sweetness to regular sugar but has 40% fewer calories. Interestingly, while technically a carbohydrate, xylitol is classed as low-carb as it does not contain fructose and hence has minimal impact on blood sugar levels. This makes xylitol a natural alternative for diabetics with its glycaemia index rating of only 7 vs 60-70 for regular sugar.

We recommend that xylitol products be used in a 1 part xylitol to 1 part sugar equivalent. Not recommended for baking situations where raising is needed -eg breads. Excessive consumption of xylitol in adults and children may induce a mild laxative effect so please use in moderation and as recommended.

DO NOT SERVE XYLITOL OR ANY PRODUCTS CONTAINING XYLITOL TO PETS.

What is Stevia?
Stevia rebaudiana, a plant native to Brazil and Paraguay in South America, has been consumed as a sweetener and sugar substitute for centuries. Stevia has seen a meteoric rise in popularity in the last two decades, with hundreds of foods and beverages around the world using stevia as a zero-calorie alternative to sugar!

Health Benefits of Stevia:
Extensive studies have concluded that stevia is safe to use in daily consumption. Stevia can help control diabetes, hypertension and obesity when used as part of a healthy lifestyle. Stevia is packed with nutrients and antioxidants and contains zero calories. It is low-glycemic and has no effect on blood sugar levels, making it an excellent choice for people who are ready to be in control of their health!

Stevia Individual Packets:
Now in convenient, single serving packets, it is easier than ever to enjoy stevia everywhere: at home, at work or on the go! 1 packet = 2 teaspoons of sugar, the perfect amount to add to a single portion for the sweetness you love!

How to Use Health Garden Stevia:
Stevia is recommended for use in beverages and liquids due to its ability to dissolve quickly and easily. Add stevia to your favorite hot drinks such as coffee, tea or hot chocolate, or use stevia in cold drinks like lemonade, cocktails and sparkling water. Stevia can also be added to smoothies, yogurt, homemade sauces, marinades and salad dressing. Try it in a variety of foods until you discover what works for you!

About Xylitol - A Great Choice For DIABETICS

Xylitol is a natural occurring polyalcohol found in most plants, fruits, vegetables and hardwoods. It has a similar sweetness to regular sugar but has 40% fewer calories. Interestingly, while technically a carbohydrate, xylitol is classed as low-carb as it does not contain fructose and hence has minimal impact on blood sugar levels. This makes xylitol a natural alternative for diabetics with its glycaemia index rating of only 7 vs 60-70 for regular sugar.

We recommend that xylitol products be used in a 1 part xylitol to 1 part sugar equivalent. Not recommended for baking situations where raising is needed -eg breads. Excessive consumption of xylitol in adults and children may induce a mild laxative effect so please use in moderation and as recommended.

DO NOT SERVE XYLITOL OR ANY PRODUCTS CONTAINING XYLITOL TO PETS.

description: Stevia is a completely safe, all-natural sweetener extracted from the herb Stevia rebaudiana. This herb has been used as a sweetener and natural remedy for over 1,500 years by native communities in Paraguay, Brazil, and Bolivia. US-FDA and Health Canada have approved Stevia for use as a sweetener and a food-additive. description:
What Is It?

Erythritol is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the “sugar alcohol” family, which means it’s derived naturally from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, erythritol does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. That makes it a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Erythritol VS Sugar

Erythritol is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike many sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some people say there is a mild cooling sensation instead. However, while sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, erythritol is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love erythritol. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but erythritol is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using erythritol in place of sugar. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers.

How Do You Use It?

You can use confectioners erythritol just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of powdered erythritol for every 1 cup of powdered sugar found in a recipe. A teaspoon or two in your morning coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use erythritol to your specific taste.

About Xylitol - A Great Choice For DIABETICS

Xylitol is a natural occurring polyalcohol found in most plants, fruits, vegetables and hardwoods. It has a similar sweetness to regular sugar but has 40% fewer calories. Interestingly, while technically a carbohydrate, xylitol is classed as low-carb as it does not contain fructose and hence has minimal impact on blood sugar levels. This makes xylitol a natural alternative for diabetics with its glycaemia index rating of only 7 vs 60-70 for regular sugar.

We recommend that xylitol products be used in a 1 part xylitol to 1 part sugar equivalent. Not recommended for baking situations where raising is needed -eg breads. You can use it right away, as an easy substitute for sugar in coffee or tea.  Remember, you'll only need half as much as regular sugar.

description:
What Is It?

Erythritol is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener and sugar replacement used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the "sugar alcohol" family, which means it’s a naturally derived extract from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, erythritol does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. It's a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Erythritol VS Sugar

Erythritol is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike most alternative sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some say there is a mild cooling sensation. While sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, erythritol is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love erythritol. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but erythritol is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using erythritol as a sugar substitute. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers. Plus, it’s proven safe for kids and pets too!

How Do You Use It?

Use erythritol just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of erythritol for every 1 cup of sugar in recipes. A teaspoon or two in your coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use erythritol to your specific taste.

Sorbitol powder (also known as Glucitol) is a sugar alcohol that the human body metabolizes slowly. Sorbitol is found naturally in apples, pears, peaches, and prunes. Sorbitol powder has about 60% the sweetness of table sugar.

Sorbitol Powder Benefits

Sorbitol powder is a low-calorie sweetener that is commonly used as a sugar-substitute. It is also used as a thickening agent.

description:
Sweetness is meant to be enjoyed. That's why Truvia created products meant to reduce sugar, not taste. The clean, sweet flavor contained in Truvia Natural Sweetener comes from nature in the form of the stevia leaf. Because leaves don't dissolve well in most of your favorite recipes, we extract the flavor from the stevia leaf and balance its rich sweetness with erythritol, a sweetener produced by fermentation. Erythritol is also found in fruits like grapes and pears. This gives you the white crystals you're used to with fewer calories. Truvia Cane Sugar Blend is a mix of Truvia Natural Sweetener and cane sugar, so it bakes and browns like sugar but with 75% fewer calories per serving than sugar. This 24-ounce (1.5-pound) bag comes with a twist off cap and pour-spout for easy use and simple storage.

El eritritol también se encuentra en frutas como uvas y peras. Esto te da los cristales blancos a los que estás acostumbrado con menos calorías. Yacon Syrup Overview

Yacon Syrup is a delicious sweetener that is extracted from the tuberous roots of the yacon plant (Smallanthus Sonchifolius), which is indigenous to the Andes mountains, located in South America. The Yacon plant, a species of perennial daisy, is also sometimes called llacon, strawberry jicama, Bolivian sunroot, ground pear and Peruvian ground apple. The edible part of the plant and the source of its syrup is found in the cluster of tuberous root vegetables. It has a sweet taste, similar to molasses or caramelized sugar, making it perfect for use as a natural sweetener, without the excess calories.

description: NOW Foods Stevia Extract Powder, 100 Packets Stevia is a small perennial plant native to Central and South America with a long and storied history. The Spanish conquistadors found out about Stevia during their sixteenth century exploration of Central America. They reported that the natives used the leaves of this herb to counteract the bitter taste of a popular community drink, mate, and also used it as an herbal remedy for various ailments.In 1887, Antonio Bertoni, a South American scientist, observed Indians of the Guarani tribe of Paraguay who used Stevia to flavor bitter tribal beverages. Bertoni erroneously classified Stevia as a member of the daisy family, but it was later re-assigned to the chrysanthemum family in 19 5.Twenty-five years later, two French chemists conducting research on Stevia isolated the primary constituents responsible for Stevia's properties and named them steviosides.

description:
What Is It?

Erythritol is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener and sugar replacement used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the "sugar alcohol" family, which means it’s a naturally derived extract from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, erythritol does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. It's a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Erythritol VS Sugar

Erythritol is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike most alternative sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some say there is a mild cooling sensation. While sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, erythritol is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love erythritol. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but erythritol is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using erythritol as a sugar substitute. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers. Plus, it’s proven safe for kids and pets too!

How Do You Use It?

Use erythritol just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of erythritol for every 1 cup of sugar in recipes. A teaspoon or two in your coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use erythritol to your specific taste.

description:
What Is It?

Erythritol is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the “sugar alcohol” family, which means it’s derived naturally from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, erythritol does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. That makes it a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Erythritol VS Sugar

Erythritol is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike many sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some people say there is a mild cooling sensation instead. However, while sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, erythritol is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love erythritol. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but erythritol is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using erythritol in place of sugar. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers.

How Do You Use It?

You can use confectioners erythritol just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of powdered erythritol for every 1 cup of powdered sugar found in a recipe. A teaspoon or two in your morning coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use erythritol to your specific taste.

Stevia rebaudiana, a plant native to Brazil and Paraguay in South America, has been consumed as a sweetener and sugar substitute for centuries. Stevia has seen a meteoric rise in popularity in the last two decades, with hundreds of foods and beverages around the world using stevia as a zero-calorie alternative to sugar!

Stevia Individual Packets:

Stevia is recommended for use in beverages and liquids due to its ability to dissolve quickly and easily. Add stevia to your favorite hot drinks such as coffee, tea or hot chocolate, or use stevia in cold drinks like lemonade, cocktails and sparkling water. Luo Han Guo is a perennial vine, cultivated in northern Guangxi of China. Its dried fruits are ellipse or round, with brown or snuff surface and abundant small pale and black hairs. The Luo Han Guo plant is cultivated for its fruit, whose extract is nearly 100 times sweeter than sugar and has been used as a low-calorie sweetener. The sweet taste of the fruit comes mainly from mogrosides, a group of triterpene glycosides that make up about 1% of the flesh of the fresh fruit.Through solvent extraction, a powder containing 80% mogrosides can be obtained, the main one being mogroside-5 (esgoside). description:
What Is It?

Erythritol is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener and sugar replacement used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the "sugar alcohol" family, which means it’s a naturally derived extract from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, erythritol does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. It's a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Erythritol VS Sugar

Erythritol is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike most alternative sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some say there is a mild cooling sensation. While sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, erythritol is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love erythritol. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but erythritol is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using erythritol as a sugar substitute. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers. Plus, it’s proven safe for kids and pets too!

How Do You Use It?

Use erythritol just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of erythritol for every 1 cup of sugar in recipes. A teaspoon or two in your coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use erythritol to your specific taste.

description:
What Is It?

Allulose is a 0 calorie & 0 carb sweetener used to add sweetness to just about anything!

It’s a part of the “sugar alcohol” family, which means it’s derived naturally from fruits and plants and passes through your body, untouched, much like fiber. Because it’s passed through, allulose does not affect blood sugar in most people and has 0 net carbs. That makes it a great option for diabetics, low carb dieters and anyone looking to cut calories without sacrificing sweetness!

Allulose VS Sugar

Allulose is 70% as sweet as sugar and their flavors are very similar. Unlike many sweeteners, there is no bitter or chemical aftertaste. Some people say there is a mild cooling sensation instead. However, while sugar is a 68 on the glycemic index (GI) scale, allulose is a 0! High glycemic foods cause blood sugar spikes, leading to more fat storage and hunger crashes.

Dentists love allulose. Oral bacteria feed off of sugar but allulose is shown to prevent plaque buildup, making it quite tooth-friendly!

Who Can Use It?

Anyone looking to reduce their sugar intake, lose weight or improve their health can benefit from using allulose in place of sugar. It’s a favorite among low-carb dieters, as well as sugar-free and paleo bakers.

How Do You Use It?

You can use confectioners Allulose just as you would sugar in cooking, baking and sweetening drinks like tea and coffee. We recommend 1 1/3 cup of granular allulose for every 1 cup of sugar found in a recipe. A teaspoon or two in your morning coffee works like a charm. Feel free to play around with the proportions and use allulose to your specific taste.

description: Since CocoSweet+plus is fortified with stevia, you use half as much -- much more economical than regular coconut sugar. CocoSweet Plus is an excellent replacement for brown sugar in recipes. It browns and carmelizes, just like brown sugar! How It's Done: CocoSweet Plus starts with harvesting or "tapping" the blossoms of a coconut tree. A small cut is made in the bark, allowing the sap to flow, similar to the process of harvesting maple syrup. The sap is collected, transfered to large woks and placed over moderate heat to evaporate the moisture. As the water evaporates, it transforms into a deliciously thick syrup-like substance known as a "toddy." From this form, it is further reduced to the usable crystals found in CocoSweet Plus. These golden crystals are then infused with our high-grade water-extracted stevia powder. The result is a golden sweetener, twice as sweet as sugar, with a slight hint of caramel. For first time users of stevia, note that there are actually different types of stevia on the marketplace. There's liquid stevia, stevia that you steep at home from the plant leaves and stevia powder. Stevia powder is standardized to different compounds. description: Erythritol is 70% as sweet as table sugar, so you can use it as a cup for cup (1:1) replacement for sugar in recipes. The result will be slightly less sweet than sugar. Use a little more if more sweetness is desired. What Is Erythritol? Erythritol is naturally occurring in nature, found in small amounts in foods like grapes, melons and mushrooms, and in fermented foods such as wine, cheese and soy sauce. How Is It Made? Usually made from the naturally occurring sugars in plants, that sugar is mixed with water and then fermented with a natural culture. This natural fermentation process yields erythritol, which is then filtered, allowed to crystallize and then dried. description:
Stevia is a completely safe sugar substitute, all-natural, pure and organic sweetener extracted from the herb Stevia rebaudiana. This pure stevia extract has been used as a sweetener and natural remedy for over 1,500 years by native communities in Paraguay, Brazil, and Bolivia. Greeniche stevia tablets are US-FDA and Health Canada approved intended to use as a sweetener and a food-additive. In recent years, improvements to extraction technology have helped evolve Stevia’s formulation, isolating the sweet component, Reb-A, and eliminating the bitter component, Reb-B.


The result is a delicious zero calories sweetener which is actually sweeter per unit weight than granulated sugar, but with zero carbs, zero calories, and a glycemic index value (GI value) of zero. And Stevia is the only commercially-available pure sweetener which doesn’t intensify sugar cravings. Many Stevia brands on the market cut cost by using low-purity Reb-A (usually 60-80%) resulting in a bitter aftertaste. Similarly, blending their low-quality Stevia with additives like maltodextrin, inulin, or dextrose also results in a product which does not allow consumers to enjoy the full benefits of this sweet gift of nature.


Greeniche Stevia in a raw tablet is made with 99.8% Reb-A, which is unparalleled in the world. For convenience, it comes in three forms – powder, tablets, and liquid – and is very versatile when used in cooking or baking. Greeniche Stevia sweetner will change your life, whether you’re managing diabetes or simply trying to eat and live healthier. You can take it anywhere and use it in virtually any recipe, without any guilt or counting calories. In no time, you’ll have forgotten it’s not sugar!

description: Since CocoSweet+plus is fortified with stevia, you use half as much -- much more economical than regular coconut sugar. We have kept all of the delicious flavor of coconut sugar, while lowering it's glycemic impact by infusing it with stevia. We have kept all of the flavor, while dramatically reducing calories and carbs. CocoSweet+plus is an excellent replacement for brown sugar in recipes. It browns and carmelizes, just like brown sugar! How It's Done: CocoSweet+ starts with harvesting or "tapping" the blossoms of a coconut tree. A small cut is made in the bark, allowing the sap to flow, similar to the process of harvesting maple syrup. The sap is collected, transfered to large woks and placed over moderate heat to evaporate the moisture. As the water evaporates, it transforms into a deliciously thick syrup-like substance known as a "toddy." From this form, it is further reduced to the usable crystals found in CocoSweet+ plus. These golden crystals are then infused with our high-grade water-extracted stevia powder. The result is a golden sweetener, twice as sweet as sugar, with a slight hint of caramel. Nutrition: The Glycemic Index of regular coconut sugar is only 35. With our proprietary blend of coconut sugar and stevia you are able to use half as much as regular coconut sugar, further reducing your glycemic impact.
